chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: The boss sells the Cigale; Baldwin and Langston Hughes
summary: By 1966 the boss planned to sell, Butler demanded a share of the profit, and recalls clientele including James Baldwin and Langston Hughes.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So now, we're in the early '60s now?

I'm running through '62, '63. I'm running through it and I'm coming around to '67 or '68. Now, '66, I heard rumors that the boss was going to sell the place. So now, you know, I told him if you're going to sell the place you're going to make a profit, you've got to give me some of this profit, I've been helping you make this money. So he went into this (stuff----table) because he was poor when he come in, and I helped him. I made him give me a standing account, if you come in with your party or group, somebody's coming in (inaudible) and you've got 12 of them there, and then he goes (unintelligible). And Richard Wright, by the way, he was -- that boy that wrote --
Oh, yeah, James Baldwin. Wrote those poems, 'Simpleton Heaven' --('Simply Heavenly')
Yeah, I got an autograph from him. He's
my special man. Yeah, he's my special man. It will all come back to me sometime.
